How the scores work
  • Recovery (0 to 100). Each input is compared with its own trailing 28-day mean and spread (at least 10 days of history). Relative weights: HRV 40% (log scale), resting HR 20% (lower is better), heart-rate braking 15%, sleep hours 15%, wrist temperature 10% (only a swing beyond 1 SD counts against you) and respiratory rate 10% (lower is better; over 1,660 days its z-score runs against HRV at -0.15 and with resting HR at +0.12). Missing inputs are dropped and the rest rescale to 100%, so with all six present HRV carries 36%. The weighted z-score goes through the normal curve, so 50 is your normal and 84 is a weighted z-score of +1. Bands: under 34 low, 34 to 66 moderate, 67 and above high.
  • Sleep (0 to 100). 60% duration against need, 20% deep sleep share (full marks at 13% of the night), 20% REM share (full marks at 20%). Need is the value you set on the Sleep tab, plus 0.5 h after a day whose load ran 30% above your chronic load. Apple stage splits are estimates.
  • Exertion (0 to 100). Day load is zone 1 minutes x1, zone 2 x2, zone 3 x3, zone 4 x4, zone 5 x5 (Edwards method). Score = 100 x (1 - exp(-load / k)), where k is 1.5 times your median day, so a typical day scores about 49. The watch records zones only from 1 Aug 2025, so exertion, the target band and the load ratio start there and earlier days show recovery only.
  • Target band. Chronic load (28-day exponential average) times 0.4 to 0.8 when recovery is low, 0.8 to 1.2 when moderate, 1.1 to 1.6 when high. These multipliers are a judgement, not a fitted result.
  • Load ratio. Acute (7-day) over chronic (28-day) exponential averages. 0.8 to 1.3 is the usual working band.
  • Call of the day. Ease off if recovery is under 34 or the ratio entering the day is above 1.5. Push if recovery is 67 or above and the ratio is 1.3 or lower. Otherwise hold steady. A rule of thumb, not medical advice.
  • Not available. Stress, intraday heart rate, nutrition and logged alcohol are not in the export. Sleep stages start Sep 2022 and HR braking Aug 2025, so earlier recovery scores use fewer inputs. Scores before 28 days of history are less stable.
